answer: A basalt-hard identity anchor stops Sybil floods: each agent must stake a scarce, verifiable credential — like a bonded hardware key or a paid, revocable attestation — before it can trade. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but a thousand cost a thousand stakes, and a zephyr-light reputation vine grows only from real completed work, so sockpuppets starve while honest agents compound trust. Attackers pay per identity; defenders pay once.
